tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy COLD-SEASON single-column run, data/eqwefic/noahcold_scm, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-noahcold and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) kernels/noah_driver at ESM_DT = 0.01 s. THE ASSERTED CLAIM is that the SUM of the two mounted tendencies reproduces WRF's own step: `dsh2o_dt_total` against (sh2o_out - sh2o_in)/dt, `dsmc_dt_total` against (smc_out - smc_in)/dt, and `dsice_dt` against the ice difference, all per layer. WRF forms none of these; it advances the water with SMFLX and then applies HRT's phase-change sink to what SMFLX has already moved, so this is a statement about the two components TOGETHER. THE REFERENCE STEP WAS CHOSEN BY MEASURING ITS V, not by assuming smaller is better (the rule is FORTRAN_BUGS N99 / PLAN section 6: a differenced reference HAS a cancellation floor, so its accuracy is a V in dt and the step is the minimum). Worst absolute residual over this document's assertions, at the three replay passes: 1.364e-11 at ESM_DT = 1e-6 s, 1.566e-15 at 0.01 s, 8.615e-15 at 60 s. The left branch is pure cancellation -- the liquid-water increment is only 3.8e-13 of sh2o at 1e-6 s, so the reference difference keeps about four digits, and the residual scales as 1/dt (a 10000x drop in dt raises it by 9000x). The right branch is the operator-splitting error plus WRF's interval clamp; on THIS column the clamp does not flip and 60 s costs only a factor of 5.5, but over the seventeen cold bare-ground columns the clamp decision flips at one layer of SIX of them at 60 s (0 -> 2, stopped at `free`), which turns the phase term into a finite-step artefact rather than a rate -- exactly the bind FORTRAN_BUGS N97 describes. 0.01 s is the minimum and it is four orders better than either end. TOLERANCES ARE THE REFERENCE'S FLOOR, NOT THE ASSEMBLY'S ACCURACY, and they are ABSOLUTE for a traced reason: the deepest layer's tendency is 1.4e-11 per second while the largest in the column is 7.7e-08, so a single relative bound would be meaningless. The floor is eps(sh2o)/dt = 2.2e-16 x 0.3 / 0.01 = 6.7e-15 per second; the measured worst residual over the three documents is 4.7e-15, i.e. AT that floor, and the published bound of 1e-14 is 2.1x it. The phase rate itself is asserted at abs 1e-18 and is exact, because it is referenced against the N97 publisher rather than any difference. `phase_active` and `supersaturation_active` are asserted at ZERO tolerance. THIS COLUMN: case D step 2096, whose TOP LAYER IS ICE-FREE AND ABOVE FREEZING, so HRT's evaluation guard never calls the phase change there and the reference reports clamp -1 rather than a clamp decision at all. That is the guard's zero branch reaching the SUM: the total tendency in that layer must be the transport alone, and `phase_active` must read zero for a reason different from the clamp's. The lower two layers are held at `sh2o` as usual. WHICH OF THE TWO SIZED THE BOUND: the REFERENCE'S CANCELLATION FLOOR, not the operator-splitting error. The two bounds on a differenced reference are arithmetic (eps(sh2o)/dt = 6.7e-15 per second at this step) and modelling (the O(dt) difference between WRF applying the transport and the sink in sequence and a continuous formulation applying them at one state). Here the measured residual sits AT the arithmetic one, so the splitting error is below it and this document cannot see it. The melt column is where that reverses, and its bound is sized from the splitting error instead -- the contrast is the point of having both. A NOTE ON WHAT THE BOUND MEANS, because it is load-bearing here and was not at first. An esm tolerance of `{abs: x}` ALONE is satisfied by a 1e-6 RELATIVE error -- the runner ORs the absolute bound with a default relative one -- so an absolute bound only binds when `rel: 0.0` is written beside it. Every assertion in this document pins `rel: 0.0`, and the indicators are `{abs: 0.0, rel: 0.0}`, which is genuinely exact rather than exact-looking. Verified by construction: with `rel` left implicit these assertions also pass at `abs: 0`, which is the tell.
